corrected_value.authors: Burke BL, Martens A, Faucher EH
corrected_value.title: Two decades of terror management theory: a meta-analysis of mortality salience research

decisions.location: Introduction, lines 12-16; Discussion, lines 38 and 40; Authors' contributions, line 51; References, lines 65-69
decisions.quote: Overall, the pattern of results reported in the previous section are inconsistent with the original results of Goldenberg et al. [9]. This does not necessarily mean that the original effect was a false positive, but it does suggest that (i) the effect may be substantially smaller than originally reported or (ii) that the effect is extremely sensitive to contextual factors and perhaps absent in some populations. Consistent with the former interpretation, our own reanalysis of Burke et al. ([3]; see also [11]) provides compelling evidence that the effect sizes of previous research on mortality salience may have been overestimated.
decisions.reason: In addition to conducting a new-sample laboratory replication of Goldenberg et al. (2001) Study 2 (shipped input_row_index 1093, doi:10.1037/0096-3445.130.3.427), the authors perform and report their own original-data reanalysis of the 277 mortality-salience effect sizes from the meta-analysis of Burke, Martens, and Faucher (2010) (doi:10.1177/1088868309352321) in Figure 1 and lines 13-16, converting correlations to Fisher's z scores, testing funnel-plot asymmetry with Egger's regression (z = 2.06, p = 0.039), and fitting a Vevea and Hedges selection model (chi2(1) = 47.87, p < 0.001; bias-corrected r = 0.22 vs Burke et al.'s r = 0.35). Shipped row 1093 covers only the Goldenberg et al. (2001) experiment, so Burke et al. (2010) is a genuinely absent reproduction target.
